note: Adapted from the species description of Acholotermes imbellis by Sands (1972), originally in English; the species has no soldier, and only the alate and the worker are described; measurement-table headings, figure numbers and distribution records are not translated, and some measurement values corrupted by OCR in the tables are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparison with A. chirotus and A. epius is given under those species. It differs from A. tithasus in the much greater inflation of the postclypeus in both the alate and the worker and in the ocelli being closer to the compound eye in the alate; the fore coxa of the worker bears distinct setae in A. tithasus but not in this species. The worker abdomen appears to be of the dehiscent type.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule straw yellow, pilosity yellow, fairly dense on both head and body. Postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.33. Mandibular apical teeth very long, ratio of left apical to first marginal tooth 1.00, right mandible 1.18; left accessory marginal tooth just free of the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 22.89; anterior margins of first and second marginal teeth of right mandible about equal, composite ratio 23.50. Fore tibia weakly inflated, T1/Tw 4.27, third apical spur distinct, about half the length of the other two spurs. Midgut and hindgut meet in a direction between transverse and oblique, touching the Malpighian node; valve seat lateral in the undissected abdomen; internal cushions of the valve moderately developed, surface scaly, posterior margin of each scale ornamented with minute spines; membranous wall of the valve beyond the cushions with numerous fine spines arranged in 15–20 rows, interrupted between the cushions into fringed lobes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle reduced, minute, circular, flat or slightly concave, concolorous with the head capsule; middle spot oval, slightly raised, larger than the fontanelle, also concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum pale yellowish brown; frontal mark small, flat, semicircular, dark brown; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, transverse sutures present; femora yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsolateral spiracles dark brown, sternites yellowish brown with the middle paler, ventrolateral spiracles brown; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by less than half their own minimum diameter; postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.32–0.34, posterior margin arched and not evenly rounded, median suture present but weak anteriorly. Mandibular apical teeth long, ratio of apical to first marginal tooth 0.89–0.91, right mandible 1.13–1.24; left accessory marginal tooth just free of the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 12.67–14.22; first marginal tooth of left mandible inserted slightly behind the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, anterior margins of first and second marginal teeth about equal. Head capsule pilosity uneven, not forming a felt, brown. Meso- and metanotum rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.30–0.31. Third apical spur of fore tibia distinct, about two thirds the length of the other two spurs.
